question: Ashtadhyayi, is a Sanskrit treatise on grammar, written in the 6th to 5th century BCE by _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Panini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Panini was **an Indian grammarian, who authored the **Ashtadhyayi,** a seminal Sanskrit grammar treatise, during the** 6th to 5th century BCE**.
 
• This comprehensive work offers insights into the language prevalent during Pāṇini's era, encompassing various dialects and registers spoken by an **elite group of individuals**.
 
• It also incorporates elements of the **older Vedic language** alongside contemporary dialectal features.
 
• The Ashtadhyāyī employs a derivational system to elucidate the structure of the language, illustrating how real speech emerges from abstract utterances through the addition of affixes to base forms under specific conditions.
 
• While the exact timeframe of Pāṇini's life remains uncertain, some scholars place him in the **4th century BCE,** coinciding with the era of conquests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Patanjali,** also known as Gonardiya or Gonikaputra, was a Hindu author, mystic, and philosopher. Scholars estimate that he lived between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE based on analyses of his works.
 
• **Agastya** is a revered Indian sage in Hinduism, renowned as a recluse and influential scholar proficient in various languages of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Vishvamitra **is among the most revered rishis, or sages, of ancient India and is recognized as one of the seven Brahmarshis.
